report.summary: Chunk 3 of canary.py: defines probe corpora, filler/arrival functions, and check_arrival logic.

handoff.purpose: Define probe corpora, filler helper, arrival probe builder and checker.

symbols.name: _FILLER_WORDS
symbols.note: Tuple of filler words used in padding lines.

symbols.name: _TAIL_WORDS
symbols.note: Tuple of tail words, disjoint from _FILLER_WORDS.

symbols.name: _ANCHOR_SETS
symbols.note: Tuple of anchor sets (tuples of 3 strings).

symbols.name: _SUMMARY_TARGETS
symbols.note: Tuple of target summary strings containing 'roll' or 'revert'.

symbols.name: _filler
symbols.note: Generates padding lines of random filler words.

symbols.name: ARRIVAL_PAD_LINES
symbols.note: Number of padding lines for arrival probe (40).

symbols.name: build_arrival
symbols.note: Builds a prompt with a nonce at start and a tail word at end.

symbols.name: expect_arrival
symbols.note: Returns expected correct reply for arrival probe.

symbols.name: check_arrival
symbols.note: Checks if reply contains both head nonce and tail word.

claims.text: The prompt varies every run (a probe a model has memorised measures nothing) while the checker still knows the right answer without carrying state between the two halves of a probe.
claims.why: This claim describes design intent but is not verifiable from the code in this chunk. It references a nonce-based variation and checker behavior that depends on _rng and nonce, which are defined elsewhere.

claims.text: Disjoint from :data:`_FILLER_WORDS` on purpose: the arrival tail token must not be findable anywhere in the padding, or a reply could satisfy the tail check by quoting the middle of the prompt.
claims.why: The code defines _TAIL_WORDS separately from _FILLER_WORDS, and a manual check shows no overlap between the two tuples. The claim is consistent with the code.

claims.text: Invented one-line summaries. None of these describes a real file in this repo, and none of them may contain "roll"/"revert" -- the comprehension probe's answer is defined by being the ONLY line that does.
claims.why: The claim references a 'comprehension probe' and repo contents not present in this chunk. The given tuples _SUMMARY_DECOYS and _SUMMARY_TARGETS exist, but the claim's full context (e.g., that decoys lack 'roll'/'revert' and targets contain them) cannot be fully verified without the comprehension probe implementation.

claims.text: ~40 lines of filler is roughly 800 tokens: long enough that a transport which truncates has something to truncate, and far enough under the Ollama usable input window that the probe itself never provokes the failure it measures.
claims.why: The claim about token count and Ollama input window cannot be verified from this code alone. The constant ARRIVAL_PAD_LINES is set to 40, and _filler generates 12 words per line, but tokenization is not defined here.

claims.text: A long prompt with a token at the VERY START and a word at the VERY END.
claims.why: build_arrival returns a string starting with 'NONCE-{nonce}\n' and ending with 'TAILWORD: {tail}', consistent with the claim.

claims.text: Both incidents were truncation, in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, so one token cannot catch both.
claims.why: The claim refers to incidents (Ollama HEAD-truncation, npm .cmd shim) that are not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: Requiring BOTH tokens back is what makes a single cheap probe cover both.
claims.why: The claim about coverage of incidents cannot be verified from this code alone.

claims.text: Accept only if BOTH ends of the prompt demonstrably arrived.
claims.why: check_arrival returns True only if head_ok and tail_ok are both true, which checks for nonce and tail word presence.

observations.what: check_arrival returns early with True or False strings, but does not handle the case where only one of head_ok/tail_ok is true (returns None implicitly).
The function check_arrival is defined but the chunk ends mid-function (missing return for partial match).
